Axiom: Write signatures and DbC contracts in the project's real language (for us, TypeScript), not in an agnostic pseudo-form. For a single-language project this is deliberate: exact signatures in the spec remove ambiguity for the implementer and let the typing scenario check them directly. This supersedes the former DbC-agnosticism rule. A genuinely cross-language contract still belongs in a `contracts` scope, expressed in its own interface language (schema / proto / IDL), not here.
